utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber explains the late start by quite a lot of paper to be digested, and sometimes it's better to do it before the court -- before the hearing starts. I'd like to deal very briefly with a few procedural matters first. For the first one it will not take much time, but I have to go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber would like to now give a statement concerning the Prosecution's motion to admit the statement of Witness 1 into evidence pursuant to Rule 92 quater of the Tribunal's Rules. The Chamber has considered the motion and the Chamber has taken a decision on the motion. The decision, the gist of it is, that only parts of the statements are admitted into evidence. The decision of the Chamber will be delivered in writing, and that written decision will indicate precisely which parts will be admitted and will also give the reasons for the decision. Nevertheless, the Chamber might be -- the parties might be in need of some guidance in view of the upcoming testimony of Mr. Versonnen. Therefore, I inform you already - and this is not the decision, but this is just a brief explanation of what the gist of the decision is - the parties are informed that the Chamber will admit those parts of Witness 1's statements that directly relate to the alleged abduction of this witness and his wife. Not necessarily to include all the details of ill-treatment that is dealt with in these statements, ill-treatment on that day -- or I should rather say during that night. Further, the parties are informed that the Chamber has in one respect not finally made up its mind, that is, as to what extent those portions of the statements that deal with forced labour, digging trenches, whether that should be admitted or not be admitted. This is -- this concludes this statement, and again I emphasise that it's mainly for guidance of the parties that we give this statement because we want to write down our decision in detail. Having dealt with that, I move on to another procedural matter which is the deadline for the Defence to respond to the admission of P1212, which is the Human Rights Watch report. We have invited the submissions of the Defence, but we didn't give any deadline for that. The Chamber has in mind to put a deadline Thursday, close of business, that's tomorrow. Is that -- would that -- I see that it does not find strong opposition, therefore the deadline is set at Thursday, this week, at close of business. Then the next matter is there was an exhibit, P1228, that is, if I could call it a Dunjic exhibit. The Chamber would like to know whether there's any objection against admission of P1228.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you mind if we return to that a little later in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- it's a photograph. I take it then that you'll come back to it soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We want an opportunity just to check the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I move on to the -- as a matter of fact, it's a photograph of two ladies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do recall, it's most unlikely that we will object to it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but we will hear further from you. Then I move on to the next item, that is, P1181 has been uploaded again, but now in a slimmed-down version and it is now on e-court under 65 ter number 2173. We're not at this moment discussing admission of that, but the Chamber would like to give to the Defence an opportunity to verify whether all elements of P1181 has now in a new version been uploaded, whether all documents that were already exhibited are taken out, and whether no new ones are added so that we could then proceed and replace P1181 by this newly uploaded, slimmed-down version. Then next issue I'd like to briefly deal with is the latest disclosure discussion. In view of the next witness, Mr. Guy-Smith, the Chamber received courtesy copies of two letters you've sent to the Prosecution, one before you had received the English translation, one after you had received the English translation. This appears to be exculpatory evidence. Of course the Chamber hasn't seen it. And I think it was our latest ruling on the matter that if material lately disclosed was inculpatory, that consent of the Defence should be obtained before following the Rules and disclose it to the Chamber as well. I've got no idea what it is. I also, for very practical reasons, would like to inquire with the Defence whether the Defence considers it where we have received, I would say, in one line what the information is about, whether it makes any sense to disclose this material to the Chamber, as the Rules require. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I think it makes sense to disclose the information to the Chamber, as the Rule requires.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Because I'm sure it's also going to be at some point the subject matter of some other type of discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that the original is in German?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You may, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as before, when it's in German we were not in a position to provide a translation. I trust that that's not going to be a problem at all I don't think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber has no problems in reading German.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There is a translation in English, we don't know of the accuracy of the translation but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be good that this translation would be provided to the Chamber as well, so that we -- although we are not the ones to check, but it would be obvious errors in there, then we might notice that. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At some point - and I'm very much in the Trial Chamber's hands as to when that point most conveniently arises - but certainly at some point prior to cross-examination it's going to be necessary to have some discussion about this document, and it might be the most convenient thing would be for the Trial Chamber to have an opportunity to look at it over the first adjournment and for the matter then to be dealt with after evidence in chief has been concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, is there any possibility that German and preferably also English version of the newly disclosed material is available for the Chamber during the next break?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's electronically on its way as we speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's good. Then finally, a new revised version with as far as Legal Officer of Chambers could verify with correct redactions of the 92 ter statement of Witness 69 has been uploaded. And at first -- the first impression is that now also the B/C/S version is -- appears to be correctly redacted. So therefore, the Defence can have a look at it under 65 ter number 1720 so that everyone is prepared if it comes to admission of this 92 ter statement. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I understand that someone from the Prosecution sat with a Legal Officer from the Trial Chamber to make sure that the two matched earlier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and of course now --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- and were given to the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it's also for the Defence to verify whether now the new version also reflects what the Defence understands was the agreement. Then, having dealt with all that, I think we could -- we could invite the Prosecution to call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next witness is Avni Krasniqi. Before he comes in, the issue is how to present the evidence. I think we had one hour on the estimate of the evidence in chief, but that was of course before he was subpoenaed and then indicted. I have -- did have an intention of trying to present it through the provisions of 92 ter, based upon a statement he gave to -- as a suspect in Kosovo on the 30th of January, 2006, under the provisions of Rule 92 ter it would have to be a statement, that is, a statement could be of course a question-and-answer statement as long as it is verified or signed by the witness or attested to by the witness. I understand the Defence is objecting to our proceeding on that basis, I assume on the basis that it's not a statement within the Rules. It's certainly not a transcript of proceedings before this Tribunal. In my submission, it could be admissible if the witness adopts it or signs it. I haven't had a chance to speak to the witness. We have provided -- I hope the witness has been given a copy of it. We attempted to get one through the Office of Legal Aid and Defence to the witness at the Detention Unit this morning in Albanian some hours ago and his lawyer has a copy of it, Mr. Pestman, as well. We would make the application if the Trial Chamber is of the view that it is admissible under that section, of course, if the witness adopts it; if not, I will call the evidence orally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. We do object to the use of the suspect interview within the provisions of Rule 92 ter, not only because in our submission it doesn't meet the requirements of sub-paragraph (a), which require it to be in the form of a written statement of evidence given by a witness in proceedings before the Tribunal or in the form of a transcript of evidence given by a witness in proceedings before the Tribunal. Moreover, the fact is that at the time this suspect interview took place, Mr. Krasniqi was the subject of a criminal investigation by UNMIK into his complicity in the abduction and death of Sanije Balaj. It followed discussions which had taken place that morning with the public prosecutor about the potential for him being declared a cooperating witness and being given an immunity, and he subsequently testified at trial and some of the testimony that he gave differed from the contents of the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Give me one second, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you were explaining the objections, and I wanted at that time already to consult with my colleagues to see whether there was any further need to -- may I take it that other Defence counsel join in the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, the circumstances under which the, at that time, suspect was interviewed are such that the Chamber considers it not to be appropriate to use the statement as put on paper at that time, to use that for 92 ter purposes. So you're invited to elicit the evidence viva voce, orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Will do. I just -- just make one small point, and that is that the only reason we were attempting to use that rather than the transcript was that -- of the trial proceedings in Kosovo was because we didn't have an Albanian transcript, whereas we had an Albanian transcript of that interview. Just to answer any concern that we were trying to prefer one over the other, we weren't. It was just a matter of there being Albanian translation or transcript. So I call Mr. Krasniqi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I could have but one moment to confer with counsel before the calling of the witness. There may be one other issue that arises as a result of something Mr. Re has just said. I just want to double-check with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to confer with my colleagues. I'm looking forward to seeing the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Madam Usher, I think with the assistance of security could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there was one issue whether Mr. Krasniqi's Defence counsel could be present. The situation in which Mr. Krasniqi finds himself at this moment, that is, being an accused in a contempt case and being a witness in the Haradinaj case -- being detained as well creates a situation in which the Chamber allows Defence counsel to be present too, but his role of course would be limited to advising his client on any procedural matter that would arise, such as the right to remain silent, not to answer questions, unless compelled by the Chamber. And then, of course, then the answers not to be used against him. These type of matters not the substance of his testimony, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is -- the matter just raised by the Trial Chamber with regard to the presence of Defence counsel with the underlying matter, that being the situation which he particularly finds himself in does cause me some concern procedurally with regard to how best appropriately to proceed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What I suggest is the following, that if Defence counsel would like to consult with his client on any such matter which arises out from the examination of him as a witness, that he'll make clear to me that he would like to raise an issue, either with the Chamber or with his client; that we then ask Mr. Krasniqi to take off his earphones. That then Mr. Pestman will be given an opportunity to explain why there's any need at that moment to intervene to the extent of course that it could be explained in public, and then we'll see how this develops. But we'll take a very cautious approach because Mr. Pestman would not be here to intervene in the examination of the witness on any other ground than in relation to the complex legal position the witness or the accused finds himself in. Is Mr. Pestman already in the courtroom? If not -- I would like Mr. Pestman to be seated in a place where there's no direct eye contact with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Krasniqi. You appear today as a witness in this courtroom, a witness who is under an obligation to answer to questions that are put to him. Unless he would incriminate himself, then that witness may address the Chamber and ask whether he should answer that question. But if you answer a question and again you're supposed to answer them unless there's any specific reason why you would not answer them, if you answer questions it should be fully in accordance with the truth; that means the truth, the whole truth, nothing less, and nothing but the truth. The solemn declaration you'll have to make for that purpose, the text of that solemn declaration will now be handed out to you by Madam Usher. And I'd like to invite you to make that solemn declaration. Could you please read that aloud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you mean I have to read this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you have to give a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, and I invite you to read this aloud because that is your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A solemn declaration. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Krasniqi. Mr. Pestman, you are present in court. You are Defence counsel for Mr. Krasniqi in another case pending before this Tribunal. The Chamber allows you to be present. Your role, however, should be limited, strictly limited, to any matter of self-incrimination. Therefore, if your client would need advice on that specific issue or when you feel that there's a strong need to advise him on these matters, you may address me. If you do so, just give me a sign. We'll then ask Mr. Krasniqi to take his earphones off, and then you can explain why there is a strong need at that moment, if need be, in private session, but then you can explain to the Chamber; and then the Chamber will decide whether or not you're allowed to consult with Mr. Krasniqi. Is that procedure clear? Mr. Krasniqi, you will first be examined by Mr. Re, who's counsel for the Prosecution in the case in which you testify, that's the case against Mr. Haradinaj, Mr. Balaj, and Mr. Brahimaj. Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Krasniqi. Is your name Avni --

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is your name Avni Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you born on the 18th of May, 1969?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you born in Vranoc, in Kosovo, and do you still live there?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is your occupation auto mechanic?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did you testify on the 16th of May this year in a trial in Kosovo against Idriz Gashi, also known as Galan or Galani, for the murder of Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to make it clear, I'm only going to ask you questions about what happened there. I'm not asking you any questions about the case in which you are an accused yourself. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Could you repeat that again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you anything about the contempt of court charge. I'm only going to ask you about what happened in Kosovo in 1998, and in particular in relation to Sanije Balaj. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to confirm that since your arrival in The Hague, I think on Saturday, you haven't had any contact with anyone from the Prosecutor's office, that's my office, except to see us in court several days ago on your initial appearance?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: You mean before I came here?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, since you got here on Saturday. I want you to confirm to the Court that you haven't spoken to anyone from the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: That day when I appeared in court myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, because we're in somewhat of a unique position, to the extent that Mr. Krasniqi is represented by counsel and there were any conversations between the Prosecutor's office and counsel which were communicated to Mr. Krasniqi and there was any communication from Mr. Krasniqi through his counsel to the Prosecutor's office, then his lawyer operates as an agent for the Prosecution's office, and that needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, of course you could seek clarification of that issue. It's not a question that Mr. Re has put to the witness at this moment himself. I also can imagine that you -- because I take it that you are -- you would like to be informed about any such matter if it has taken place. Then of course you could either ask the witness or perhaps find out in other ways which doesn't take court time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But to the extent we have already received late disclosure and there may well be other late disclosure and this could well be a Rule 68 issue and there's an agency concept that exists, I thought I should raise it now before anybody was led astray as to what anybody's or position may be because we're in such a unique situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm aware of that. I think it could be initiated before court and the Chamber even has considered whether we should inquire into it prior to the testimony of the witness. But certainly I do understand that you would like to find out and there will certainly be a way to find out. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question is directed solely to whether the witness has spoken to anyone in the Prosecutor's office before coming to court and I was seeking an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think I understand that. Mr. Krasniqi, you might be a bit disturbed in your concentration. What Mr. Re asked you is whether since you arrived in The Hague whether you had any conversation with any member of the Office of the Prosecutor, or whether you only saw them when you were in court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only saw my lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And no one from the Office of the Prosecution, I take it from this answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I met somebody from the Tribunal the first day when I came here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that was not someone from the Prosecutor's office, if I correctly understand you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question. I don't know what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to resolve this to the extent possible by agreement, Mr. Guy-Smith, and perhaps also the other questions that are -- Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just make the practical suggestion that we carry on with the witness's testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and when there's a break perhaps we can have five minutes longer than normal and we can inquire of Mr. Re for full disclosure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to be a very practical approach. Mr. Re, please proceed and let's go to the core of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will. Although I indicate there is no disclosure issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, let's go back to 1998 and May of 1998. Were you living in Vranoc in May 1998?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you working then?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Up until one month before Vranoc was attacked, I was working, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was Vranoc attacked?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Vranoc was attacked on the 29th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were you doing in the month before Vranoc was attacked?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I had a private firm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you were working up until a month before. What's the significance of that? I want to know what you were doing in the month before Vranoc was attacked.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: As I said, I had a private firm. I had trucks and I transported gravel and shingle for construction work or to build canals or things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you in the FARK or the KLA before your village was attacked?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Before our village was attacked, there was an organization carried out before the village was attacked. There were volunteers who formed a staff that would defend the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you one of those volunteers?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have arms?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: For the moment when we formed this staff, we did not have enough weapons, but weapons came I think 10 to 15 days after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Approximately when was it that you formed this -- you people formed this staff?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was in May, 14th or 15th of May, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many people were involved in forming this staff?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: In the forming of this staff you mean, well, the whole village or all the villagers were ready to protect ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In terms of numbers, how many are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, there were many, but I don't know how many because we did not have lists. But there were many volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say "many," I mean, are you talking about 10? 50? A hundred? A thousand? What sort of figures?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: About 20 or 25 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, you said about 10 to 15 days after the staff was formed you received weapons. What sort of weapons were they and where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: These were weapons that came from Albania. There were people who were authorised to go there and bring the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of weapons were they and how do you know they came from Albania? Or in other words, which people were authorised to go there and bring them?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: People went there voluntarily and they were authorised to go and get the weapons and bring them back in order to protect and help the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you go to Albania to collect weapons?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of weapons were brought back to your village, type of weapons and quantities, please?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Kalashnikovs, we called them Kalasha.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And ammunition for them?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Not a lot, whatever they could bring for those weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about heavier weapons, did you have those as well?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, there were no heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And were each of the 20 to 25 people referred to as volunteers, did each of them receive a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There were not enough to go around. Some did receive weapons, some didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have uniforms at that point?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was organizing bringing the weapons to your village?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know who did the organization. I know that the weapons came from Albania, they were collected there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was the commander of your village staff?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Din Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know who he reported to, who his leader was?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, Din had good relations with Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying he reported to Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, Din was head of this staff and he was obliged to have contacts with Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What contact was he obliged to have with Ramush?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did your village staff obtain the weapons before or after the attack on your village on the 29th of May?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Some of the weapons were there before Vranoc was attacked; after the attack, other weapons came.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who attacked your village, was it the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did they do?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They attacked at 5.00 in the morning. They burned down 42 houses and they also burned my excavator. Four civilians were killed, some people were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your statement of the 30th of January last year, you said 22 houses. Did we hear 42 or 22?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, it was 22. I saw that I confused it. I said 42, but it was 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Describe the attack. What did the Serbs do? You said they burnt down some houses, your excavator, and civilians. How did they attack?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They attacked the main points where our guards were, Gani Krasniqi, Astrit Krasniqi, and Komir Krasniqi, who protected the population because they were there, guarding the civilian population, the civilian population could escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did the -- were the guards armed with the Kalashnikovs you referred to a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they fight back when the Serbs attacked?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was their response to the Serb attack, that is, the guards, what did they do?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, their reaction was to raise the alarm and notify the people that we were being attacked, and whoever heard that an attack was being launched, they started to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before the Serbs attacked, was the village staff in control of your village of Vranoc?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did your village staff resist the Serb attack on the 29th of May; and if so, how?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There was no resistance in the proper sense of the word, because the weapons and the ammunition we had was not sufficient to react against the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And had there been a Serb or a government police station in your village?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did the Serbian officials leave your village?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: That day, at about 2.00 or 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A moment ago you said the village staff had been in control of the village before the Serb attack. What I'm asking you was: Before the village staff took control of the village, when did the Serb officials leave it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment -- one second, please. One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be a bit like the question: When did you stop beating your wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It makes the assumption in the question that there was Serb officials inside the village, at the moment as far as I understand it, there's no testimony to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had there been Serb officials in your village at any point before May 1998?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You described the Serbs attacking the village on the 29th of May. How long did the attack go and what happened -- last for, and what happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, the attack continued until midday. Some villagers came from other villages as volunteers to help us. One of them was Rrustem Tetaj, who came to assist with some of his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Rrustem Tetaj and his soldiers resist the Serbs on that day?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I did not see them when they came. I saw them later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know anything about whether they resisted the Serbs on that day, that is, whether there was a fight between the Serbs and Rrustem Tetaj and his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Rrustem came after the attack at about 12.00, that's when he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were the Serbs by then when Rrustem Tetaj and his men arrived?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The Serbs were in the village with their machinery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, what -- was there any conflict between Rrustem Tetaj and his men and the Serbs after he arrived?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did the Serbs remain in the village for?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Until 2.00 or 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it Serb police or military or a combination?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There were army people, paramilitaries, policemen, they were all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see them yourself?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of weaponry did they have?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: That day -- well, I couldn't recognise all the weapons from afar, but they had tanks and APCs, military vehicles. I couldn't recognise what handguns they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how many do you think there were or what -- how many do you think you saw there?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Many.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you give an estimate, 10, 20, 100, 500?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, I think there were a hundred, 150 soldiers and policemen all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: After this attack and houses were burnt down and people were killed, did the Serbs leave the village?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it then again under the control of the village staff after the Serbs left?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you had become one of the volunteers. I want to ask you about the formalisation process of arming and becoming part of the KLA or the FARK. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber about that.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question again, please, it's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you become involved in the KLA or the FARK yourself?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: In the beginning I was in the KLA. The commanders then agreed with each other and then I joined the FARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just give us some dates for this, when it was that you were in the KLA and then you joined the FARK.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I joined the FARK after the military barracks were established, but I don't know the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were these the military barracks in Baran?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, one of them in Baran and the other one in Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the one in Baran, was that in the school?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you're not sure of the dates, what about the seasons? Was it summer? Autumn? Spring?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was July I think, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your assignment?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Some people were selected to be soldiers, some were selected to be military policemen. The commander of the police was Hasan Gashi and the military police had the duty to keep the army under control so that the soldiers would be disciplined. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying that you joined the military police?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have a uniform?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was it? Describe the uniform.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was a multi-coloured uniform, it was a German uniform. Some people had different uniforms from mine. Not all the people in the army had the same uniform because there were not enough uniforms to go around.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many people were in your military police unit?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know the number. Well, I would say about 15 or 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about patches, did members of the military police unit wear patches; if so, what were they?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The patches were KLA patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you wear a KLA patch yourself?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I had it on my uniform, but I remember that I had one on my cap.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What weapons were you and the military police issued with and using?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The military police unit you've been referring to, was that based in the military barracks in Baran?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was based in the Shkolla e Kuqe, the red school, that's where the barracks were, but the military police was in a different place from the main barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was it, how far away was it and in what building was it, that is, the military police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: We call it Shkolla e Kuqe, which is, the red school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the barracks, that is, the soldiers and the military police there in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Nazif Ramabaja, Musa Draga and Esat Ademi were in Baran, while the commander of the police was Hasan Gashi.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was Nazif Ramabaja the commander?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: In the military barracks in Baran, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just describe very briefly your duties as a military police officer, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I was not an officer, I was just a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do as a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Our tasks were to keep the army under control. They were not allowed to do whatever they wanted. That was what we had to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now about Sanije Balaj. Were you related to Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your family relationship to Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: As far as I know, my father is a cousin of her uncle's on her mother's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How well did you know her?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I knew her from before. I knew the whole family.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying you knew her by her first name and she knew you by your first name?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I knew Sanije Balaj, her brother Shaban Balaj, and her relatives, I know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about what happened to Sanije Balaj. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber about your seeing her at the military barracks and what happened. Okay?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about Sanije Balaj and what happened to her, okay? And I want you to go to a day when you saw her at the military barracks and I want you to start at the beginning. Where were you when you saw her the first time on that day?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Okay. There were some of us, policemen, we were sitting and drinking a soft drink and we saw two policemen who had taken Sanije Balaj and they were accompanying her to the barracks. They were taking her somewhere in the barracks to Nazif Ramabaja, probably, but I don't know where they took her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: What do you mean when?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it 1998? When was it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When in 1998? You said you were a military policeman there in July. When was it in relation to when you started working there as a military policeman.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It must have been in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it day?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were the two police who were taking Sanije Balaj to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I can't remember who stopped her and who took her there -- well, the person who interrogated her was Cufe Krasniqi. The thing I can speak about is only after she was interrogated and on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were you with when you saw her being brought into the barracks?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I was together with some soldiers, Hysen Ukaj, Ahmet Ukaj, Nexhat Gashi and other policemen, some of them were killed and others I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was Sanije Balaj and the two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The witness has just mentioned the names of three people. I wonder if we could have some clarification about the second name he mentioned and its relationship to a witness who testified yesterday. I see the way it appears on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that the Ahmet Ukaj you referred to yesterday, is he the Ahmet Ukaj from Vranoc who was born in July 1968 [Realtime transcript read in error "1958"] and testified here, I think, yesterday. Is it the same person?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, this date, 1958, I don't think this is the Ahmet I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I said -- it appears as 1958, I thought I said 1968.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Okay, yes, 1968.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The same Ahmet Ukaj who was in the military police?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was Sanije Balaj and these two other police coming from when you saw them going to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There was a kiosk or a shop where we bought things there, food, and drinks, cigarettes, and they brought her in that direction and went towards the school where the military barracks were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, one of the previous questions triggered by Mr. Emmerson still is puzzling me. You asked whether it was the same person, and since the year of birth was corrected to 1968, I think this witness would know that we're referring to a person of approximately 40 years old. Now, you suggested that the witness would be aware that he was a witness in this courtroom. Could we verify whether the witness is aware of that, because otherwise we have only 40 years old, nothing else, and that might be a not-too-solid basis to draw such conclusions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, do you hear Judge Orie's question, are you aware that someone called Ahmet Ukaj born in 1968 testified here yesterday and he was from Vranoc and is that the same person you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are two questions, the first whether you are aware that he gave testimony. You were aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I saw him on TV last night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you were aware that she was -- Sanije Balaj was interrogated by Cufe Krasniqi. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: At the place we were sitting, we were in front of the school and Cufe was in inside with her in a room. And I don't know what they talked about or how he interrogated her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know how she came to leave the room?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. When Idriz Gashi, Galani, came and he went inside and spoke to Cufe, I don't know what they talked about, then Galani came outside with Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Let's go back. Did you know Idriz Gashi, Galani, before that day?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, Idriz Gashi, Galani, did you see him go into the school?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Tell the Court what you saw.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I saw Idriz Gashi entering the office where Cufe was with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did he come from to go into that office?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He stopped the car at the kiosk. He stopped there for two or three minutes. Somebody told him that a person had been arrested, and when he heard that he went inside. So he went to a side door of the school. That's where the entrance was, the gate. I cannot say that I could see him entering the office when the entrance was on another side, but I could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know why he went to that office?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see him come out of the office?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: When he came out with Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Describe what you saw when he came out with Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He came out with Sanije Balaj. He had a little notebook, it looked like a white notebook, and he was swearing at us. He said, How can you allow a person who is a suspect and that is interrogated and this person has in her notebook names of criminals, Serb criminals. We knew some of the names who were policemen in Peje. I remember some of the names, and we kept silent, we didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember the names now?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Some of them I remember of the Serb policemen, such as Salipur [phoen], Borelovici [phoen], and I don't know the surnames, I'm sorry, but there were five or six Serb names that he mentioned but I remember these two best.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he show you the names in the book or just tell you the names were in the book?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, he pointed to the notebook and he said, Look at the names and look at the phone numbers, but we could not see what was written there from where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was Sanije Balaj when he was talking to you and, you said, swearing at you?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: She was behind him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there anyone else with him?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What weapon did he have?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He had a Kalashnikov and a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he in uniform?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Describe his uniform.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: That day he was wearing a black uniform with a cap, but it was not black, it was of a different colour and with the KLA patch on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, did I understand "a black uniform" or "the black uniform," what did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That day the uniform he was wearing was black, but his cap was not black, it was of a different colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was his position? You said he was wearing a KLA -- he had a KLA patch. What was his position in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He was commander of Lugu i Drinit, that's what he said, that he had been appointed by Ramush Haradinaj and Sali Veseli and we respected him as the commander of Lugu i Drinit, who contributed and who was a good commander. But look what happened later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was Ramush Haradinaj's position at that time?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: At that time Ramush Haradinaj was commander of the Dukagjin Plain. For a short period Tahir Zemaj was commander and then after that again Ramush Haradinaj was commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long was Sanije Balaj inside the school before you saw her come out with Idriz Gashi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: She stayed in the barracks for about one hour, one and a half hours, because her cousin was waiting for her, to take her home.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did she leave with her cousin to go home?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, no. No, it's wrong -- well, she was waiting for her cousin to come and take her home, but it happened differently, as you know, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's what I want you to tell the Court about what happened differently. Now, Iber Krasniqi, was he there? Iber Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was -- what about Cufe Krasniqi, was he there when she came out of the building with Idriz Gashi, Galani?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Cufe was inside the building with Sanije Balaj when Idriz Gashi came, and Idriz Gashi went inside. I don't know, I was not there, to tell you what they talked about. But what I know is that Idriz Gashi and Sanije Balaj came outside. Whether Cufe went towards the school, I don't know, because from the place we were sitting we could not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, after Idriz --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm in the Trial Chamber's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re, you are, we had a late start and therefore if you could find a suitable moment in the next --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's a suitable moment for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll have a break and resume at 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before we broke you were -- you said that Sanije Balaj was outside with Idriz Gashi waiting for her cousin to take her home. Now, I'm just trying to work out whether it appeared to you from that that she was actually free to leave at that point.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No. Sanije Balaj remained inside with Cufe Krasniqi. When Idriz Gashi arrived, Sanije Balaj remained inside because she was allowed to return home.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Look. What I'm just after is when you said you saw them outside, did you see Cufe Krasniqi say anything about whether or not she was allowed to stay or go?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: We were outside, then we learned that she was allowed to return home and then her relatives are waiting for her to take her home, but in fact she remained inside with Cufe, in the office of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether Cufe released her?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, we knew that, that she had been released.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That Cufe had released her?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know who released her from the military barracks, Nazif Ramabaja or somebody else, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether Cufe had any role in her release?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, let's just go back to where you were outside when she came outside. What happened after Idriz Gashi had the notebook, started swearing at you, and told you about the names of the Serbian police in that notebook, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: We went out, Sanije Balaj and he had that notebook in the hand, and he said, How do you allow these to be released and return home? And he read out the names of the Serbian police to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And then what did you do, what did Idriz Gashi do and what did Sanije Balaj do?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Sanije Balaj was behind Idriz Gashi. Idriz Gashi ordered me, said, Take it to the Gllogjan headquarters, and then I obeyed to -- his order and then we went to Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Gllogjan headquarters of what?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was the command of Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did Idriz Gashi order you to take Sanije Balaj to Ramush Haradinaj's headquarters in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you obey his order?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Because I couldn't say no because he was my superior and I had to obey his order, and anyone else who would have been told so would have done so as I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was he reporting to?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Who he was reporting to? Can you please repeat the question once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was Idriz Gashi reporting to that you had to obey his orders?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He was reporting to the UCK command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said earlier that Ramush Haradinaj was the commander in the Dukagjini Zone. Was Galani reporting to Ramush Haradinaj or someone else?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, he was a military superior and he was appointed to that post and he was reporting to Ramush Haradinaj and Sali Veseli and we respected that. We don't know to whom he reported or with whom he had any contact because we were in the command of Baran.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who appointed him to that post, do you know?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, we did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he say why you had to take Sanije Balaj to Ramush Haradinaj's headquarters in Gllogjan, that is, what the reason was to go there?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, he did not give any reason, and whether it would be sent to Ramush Haradinaj but that it would be sent to the Gllogjan staff and we never asked him why or how.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A moment ago you said: "I obeyed the order, then we went to Gllogjan." Did you actually get to Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No. Probably you understood it not in the proper way. I did not go to Gllogjan. He sent a car to send her to Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't quite understand your last answer. Can you clarify that? You said: "He sent a car to send her to Gllogjan." Who is "he"?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He ordered me to take the car and then drive Sanije Balaj and Idriz Gashi to Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there a car?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, it was the car of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of car?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was a red Golf.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who got into the car?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was myself, Sanije Balaj, and Idriz Gashi.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was driving?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was Sanije Balaj and where was Idriz Gashi in the car?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Sanije Balaj was in the back seat of the car and Idriz Gashi was in front seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you drive in the direction of Gllogjan from Baran?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was Sanije Balaj aware that you were taking her to Ramush Haradinaj's headquarters in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was she aware of why she was being taken there after --

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, probably because she was going to be interrogated or I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there a connection with the notebook that Idriz Galani -- Idriz Gashi, Galani, had in which he said were the names of Serb policemen, was there a connection between that and the trip to Gllogjan for the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At this time I'm going to interpose an objection; it calls for speculation at this time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you repeat the question again, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps in a way in which no speculation is sought.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of any connection between the notebook, the Serb names, and the trip to Gllogjan for the interrogation at Ramush Haradinaj's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, apart from the fact that that question -- apart from the fact that that question is leading --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, one second, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The way it's put now, it's leading. I mean, we're shortly going to get to the point where the bell -- where it will be impossible to unring this bell, but we haven't reached that point yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, it is a leading question. Would you please reformulate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said probably she was going to be interrogated. What was she probably going to be interrogated about as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: About the notebook with the names of the Serbian policemen, and I'm sure that it would have probably been about that notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How far did you get on your drive between Vranoc and Ramush Haradinaj's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: We went about 3 to 4 kilometres, 5 maybe, I don't know. We were driving the car and the road was -- it was not an asphalted road, but that it took us probably 20 minutes or something like this, but I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you stop?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. When I was driving the car in the direction of Gllogjan and then was told, Stop the car here, I stopped the car. And he spoke with Sanije Balaj. They went outside the car. And after 40 minutes we -- sorry, after 40 seconds we reached to -- heard shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you stop? What was the location where you stopped?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was at Lugu i Isufit, as we call it in the mountains of Vranoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why -- do you know why you were ordered to stop the car there?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said they went outside the car and about 40 seconds you heard shots. Where did they walk to?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, I did not get out of the car. I remained inside the car. Only Idriz Gashi and Sanije Balaj got off the car, went out of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Sanije Balaj come back?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No. And I did not believe that this would have occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did they walk to?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They went in the direction of the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said in the direction of the mountains. What was the -- were there plants there like trees or bushes or any geographical features?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The area was mountainous and I don't know what was the aim of taking her there, it was his order, and they got her out of the car and in 40 seconds I heard three shots. Then when returned from the mountains I said, What did you do? And he looked at me that I was a bit confused and he said, Don't worry, the same -- he said, If you say something, then the same fate will happen to you as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You heard some shots. What was he armed with?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He had Kalashnikov and a white pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was he doing with the pistol when he came back?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The cartridge was still there, and when he came inside the car and then he just put the pistol down slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were the shots you heard Kalashnikov shots or pistol shots?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They were shots from the pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was anyone else around?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: We saw some shepherds around who were there with their cattle, but they were very far away. And I do not know who might have been there in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there any children?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you remember how many?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what happened when he got back in the car and said, Don't tell anyone or you'll suffer the same -- the same fate will happen to you, what did you do then? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: After that, I took him to Baran and I left the car of the staff. I took my own car and then went home. I was very concerned and upset and I went home to rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether -- just going back for a moment, whether Idriz Gashi spoke to the children that you said were around when he came back from shooting Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Idriz Gashi spoke to any of the children before or after going off with Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I do not remember before or after, but I remember that he yelled them and then said, Go away, told them, Go away, but I can't remember whether it was before or after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was Sanije Balaj wearing?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: She was wearing a short skirt, white and black; she had white shoes, but I cannot remember anything -- any colour -- any other colour of her clothes because I probably didn't watch very closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph and ask you if you can tell us anything about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we please be shown photo Exhibit P804, it's the fifth photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's going to come up on the screen, but while that comes up I'm going to ask you: Did she have a handbag or any accessories with her?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did she take it with her when she went with Galani?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Now, there's a photograph on the screen of a dress. Was that the dress she was wearing or does it look like the dress she was wearing?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It might have probably been that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does it look like it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, black and white, it seems so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the notebook, where was the notebook? What did Galani do with this notebook he had before?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Galani took the notebook with him and I don't know any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, you said you went home. What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I took Galani to Baran. Then I took my own car and went home to rest. I was very upset and very concerned, and this is the reason I went back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know where Galani went after that?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No. I don't know where Galani went, but afterwards I heard that he met Mete and then he quarrelled with him, and then Mete asked him, Where did you leave that person? He said -- he said he sent her to Gllogjan. And then he had a few words with -- quarrelled with him because then he was not allowed to -- he -- she could not come back to the military barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mete, is that Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it Mete who told you about this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm reluctant to interrupt, but that really is a very leading question. It would be extremely helpful if Mr. Re could explore the basis for the witness's knowledge of this particular interchange for reasons that will become apparent.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's what I was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in a leading way. You could have asked who has told you or how did you learn. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. I didn't realize that was an issue, but okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What's your relationship with Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He's my brother, Mete is my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And he's deceased?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He was killed after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mete told you, according to what you just said, that he had quarrelled with Galani. When did he tell you this and when did he say that they had quarrelled?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Mete had quarrelled with Galani because of the murder of Sanije -- the killing of Sanije Balaj, and because they quarrelled, then Galani at one point said, I killed her, there's nothing you can do about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we must be at cross-purposes because the objection was to Mr. Re specifically putting to the witness that his brother Mete had told him about that conversation, and that's exactly what he's done the second time. So it must be that he mustn't have understood my objection to the leading question. Could he please just explore with this witness what the basis is of his knowledge of that conversation between Mete and Galani.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If it's not clear, Mr. Krasniqi, who told you about the quarrel between your brother Mete and Galani?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There were also other policemen there when they quarrelled. It was not only Mete and Galani, and they debated and it was a big deal why she was killed in that way. And then he said, I killed her, what can you do now? If someone asks about her, then you tell my name and tell those people who killed her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It has been like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who told you about the quarrel between your brother Mete and Galani? Was it your brother or someone else or a combination of people who told you about that quarrel?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This has been a combination of all people who had heard about it. It was like this, and also Galan also told about the presence of the police there because he said he had killed her and if someone asks who killed her just tell them my name. He told it not only in the presence of Mete but there were other policemen there. I do not know who else was there from the policemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, there seems to be the following problem. You describe a situation where your brother and Galani are quarrelling, and as you said in the presence of policemen. Now, were you present when this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then who told you that this happened? Was there one person or were there more persons who told you about this event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Mete came home, he told me about this, that it happened like this, why Galani killed her. And then he told me how it happened and how he killed her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did anyone else also tell you the same story or was he the only one who told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it was Mete, but I also heard it from other people, but I cannot remember who was from the policemen there when they had that conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Sorry, I have also a short question, Mr. Krasniqi. It was translated that you said: "When Mete came home, he told me about this, that it happened like this, why Galani killed her." Did he tell you the reason why Galani had killed her or the fact that Galani had killed her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he came he wanted to know -- he quarrelled with Galani there and Galani had told me, and this is -- he said Galani told me this and this and where -- the place where she was killed. This had been -- Mete had wanted to know from him whether she was killed or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You mentioned before a person called Sali Veseli. Was there any mention of his name in the context of anything you've just said?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Galani mentioned that in Baran, in the presence of the police, and in many other places he had said that he had killed her upon the order of Sali Veseli. I don't know what that order might have been or from whom he got the order to kill her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was the discussion you're referring to between Mete and Krasniqi -- Mete Krasniqi, your brother, and Galani? Where did they have this quarrel?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I do not know whether it happened in Vranoc or in Baran, I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, what happened with burying her body? Did you participate in burying her body?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. How did you come to do that?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Iber Krasniqi and Galani came by car, they took me, and we went to bury her. Iber Krasniqi took us to the place. Galani and myself went there. Galani was armed that night. I went and he -- he actually showed me the place where she was killed, he said, It's there, and he said, We have to bury her. And Hysen Ukaj, Ahmet Ukaj and Zymer Ukaj came at this moment -- or maybe it was Zymer Ademi, I cannot remember the name quite well, cannot remember his family name. And probably there had been also two other people but I don't know them and I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long after Idriz Gashi shot Sanije Balaj did you go with Iber and Galani, that is, Idriz Gashi, to bury the body, was it that day or another day?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I'm not sure about this, whether it was that day or another day or it might have been sometime when it's -- became dark, maybe it might have been 7.00 or 8.00 in the evening, I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said Hysen Ukaj and Ahmet Ukaj and someone else maybe it's Ademi were there and two other people, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: We went to bury her and they -- a child had told them that a killing had occurred. And now I recall that we went to bury her the same night, and they came to see who was killed. And at the time when they came, Galani was there with a Kalashnikov and was pointing the Kalashnikov at them and said, Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you when he was pointing the Kalashnikov at them and yelling, Stop -- I'm sorry, and saying, Stop?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I was burying Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: At that moment he ordered Ahmet Ukaj to come and help out, to bury her, in order not to destroy the body or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you were burying the body. How were you doing that? I mean, were you digging a hole, for example?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: With what?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: With a spade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you get the spade from?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The spade was in the car, Iber and Galani had the spade in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you go with them to bury the body?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Because they took me. Galani said, You should come, and then we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did they collect you from?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They collected me from my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
