utterances.text: Let's just go back to the burying. You said he -- Galani ordered Ahmet Ukaj to come and help you. What did Ahmet Ukaj do?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Ahmet Ukaj came and helped me and we buried her. Then we left the scene and we went each to his own home.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Galani help you bury the body?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Because he did not help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you return to the scene? Did you return to the scene?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: How --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That is, where the body was buried.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, not that day. I do not understand the question quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. You said you helped to bury the body. Let's go to that. When you buried it, how deep was the hole and how effectively buried was she?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was not deep. It was 30, 40 centimetres. It was not deeper than that. It was a soft ground, soil, and then we took soil from that area and then we covered her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you had heard shots and the body was there and she was wearing the dress you've identified. Where had she been shot?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I did not see her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you helped bury her.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, it was night. It was very difficult to see where the shots were and it was in a forest amongst the trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you left there. You went home. You said you didn't go back the same day. Did you go back to the place where she was buried?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Only on the day we went to rebury her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How --

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Unearth her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long after the day you buried her the first time did you go back to rebury her?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: After three days, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you come to go back to rebury her?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: We were at the school, Iber Krasniqi and myself and many other policemen, and Idriz Gashi came with Toger and two other people whom I did not know. And he pointed his finger at me and said, Come here. Because of security I took Iber Krasniqi with me, and then we went and unearthed her together with two other persons, and then we put her in the jeep of Toger.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. You said you were with -- you were at the school and Idriz Gashi came with Toger. How did they come?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They came by jeep and parked it in front of the school building, and then Galani addressed me and said, Come here. When I went there he said, We should go and take the body and take it to another place. And I took Iber Krasniqi with me just to help me and because of security concerns. Then we took her -- blanket.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just go back for a moment. I'll come back to that. You said there was a jeep. Whose -- Toger and Idriz Gashi came in a jeep; whose jeep was it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What colour was it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was driving it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Togeri.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you seen the jeep before?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you take Iber Krasniqi with you for security reasons? What was your concern?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I was concerned because I thought it's better than Iber Krasniqi is better -- is present there as well to see what will happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But you said you had security concerns; what were they?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: That he should come there with me and see what will happen or if something will happen to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's just go back to where we were a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And could the witness please go a little closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said Toger drove you and Iber Krasniqi and Idriz Gashi back to where the body was. What did you do? You said before you had a shovel or a spade. Did you have a spade when you came back to the scene again?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, the spade -- well, I don't really remember it, whether we had a spade or we were just taking the soil by hands. I don't really remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There was a blanket. What did you do with the blanket?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, we put the body in the blanket, and then we put it at the trunk of the jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was Toger -- stop there. I withdraw that question. Who dug the body up? Who helped you?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was me and Iber Krasniqi and two other people - I didn't know them. Toger was sitting in the car, in the jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you go with them to dig up this body and put it in Toger's -- and put it in the jeep that Toger was driving? What was the reason for digging the body up?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, the reason was I really didn't know what purpose -- on what purpose it was done like that. Idriz Gashi said that they were sending her to some other place just to be in a safer place, and I think this was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On whose orders was this being done?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was order by Galani.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was Galani's relationship to Toger?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Idriz Gashi tell you why Toger was there with him?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that Idriz Gashi said they were sending her to some other place just to be in a safer place. What was the safer place they were taking the body to?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where they took the body to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were you told about where this safer place may be?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know. We went to Vranoc, and then I don't know what direction they took.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we've got to the point where the body was in a blanket. Whereabouts in the jeep was it put?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: At the trunk of the jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Where did you all go from there with the body? And I take it -- and did Toger drive the jeep?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. Then we were sent to Vranoc, and I don't know where they went after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. You're in a car with Toger, Idriz Gashi, Iber Krasniqi, two people you don't know, and a body in the trunk. You went to -- all of you went to Vranoc; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, Idriz Gashi stayed in Baran, whereas me and Iber Krasniqi, we were ordered to get on the jeep and Toger was with two other people, whereas Idriz Gashi remained in Baran. We were sent back to Vranoc. I don't know where they went after this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That was my slip. I apologise. Did Toger drive you back to Vranoc or did you make your own way back?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, we were driven to Bistrica and I don't know -- we were dropped off there and I don't know where he went after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which road did Toger take when he dropped you off in Bistrica?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, there is a crossroad there where we were dropped off and there is a way going to Baran and another road going to our house. However, I don't really know whether they got the direction to Gllogjan or to Baran. I don't really know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was in charge when Toger drove you there in his jeep and waited in the car when you, the others, went and dug up the body?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Misstatement of the evidence. The possessive noun.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The jeep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The jeep, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was in charge when Toger drove you there in the jeep, the black jeep, picked up the body, drove you back, and drove off with the body in the trunk?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, who was in charge? Idriz Gashi was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was in charge in the car when Toger drove you in the jeep to dig up the body and then drove off with it after dropping you off? Who was in charge then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, the question calls for speculation, first of all. It also assumes that someone can be in charge of a car. Mr. Re has more than once got information that an individual named -- as far as this witness is concerned named Toger was driving the jeep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that doesn't -- Mr. Re, you may ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please answer the question, Mr. Krasniqi. Who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It also -- I'm sorry, I apologise, it also assumes facts that are not in evidence that anyone was in charge, and therefore it's also leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith, the objection is overruled. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What am I supposed to say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, to give an answer to the question. The question was when you were in the car whether there was anyone; and if so, who decided or gave instructions or -- I mean at every corner you can turn to the left or the right. Was anyone saying, Let's go to the left or to the right, or was it the driver who silently decided where to go. Could you tell us how this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Galani, when he was dropped off in Galan [as interpreted], the order was that Togeri should take the corpse, and then I was driving from this place to the scene of the crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said "the order was ..." Did someone give such an order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Galani had ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Galani go with Toger as far as you know when Toger drove off with the body in the back of the jeep?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know. What I don't know I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What's Toger's name?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: At that time we didn't know the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know his name now?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Now I do know it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, what is it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: His name is Idriz Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever hear what happened to the body after Idriz Balaj, Toger, took it away in the jeep?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No -- well, after the corpse was taken from that place, then the relations between Galani and Mete were not anymore the ones they used to be. I've never have good relations with these persons anymore later this moment and I don't know what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your feeling and the feeling of other soldiers towards Toger, that's Idriz Balaj, at the time when you took Iber Krasniqi with you for security reasons?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection, relevance as to the feeling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And apart from that, what the feeling of others is, Mr. Re, is not something the witness could tell us. I think he could tell us about how he saw other people reacting, and that is a relevant question. So please put that question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did other people react to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And of course the witness himself because it was part of the question as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you yourself react towards Toger?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, we did nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you took someone with you for security reasons when you went with him in his jeep?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sorry the jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I rise for an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that -- the jeep has been corrected by now. Is there another objection, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He's indicated how he -- he's already I indicated how he reacted to Toger, so it's -- it's been asked and answered. He did nothing. How did he react to Toger, he did nothing. I know precisely what Mr. Re is trying to lead him to, but he's already got his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re is allowed to ask the question in a different form, as he did. Mr. Re, you may repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question was: You said you took someone with you for security reasons when you went with Toger in the black jeep.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber why you felt the need to take someone with you for security reasons when you went with Toger in the black jeep to dig up the body?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I really -- at this point I have to object and I need to stop the transcript to go back because the reference was earlier made with regard to the issue of security reasons where --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A moment ago you said that you took Iber Krasniqi because you -- "that he should come there with me and see what will happen or something would happen to me." What did you think or fear might happen to you if you did not take Iber Krasniqi with you?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I took him just for security reasons. I wanted him to be with me there. This was the only reason I took him with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not, Mr. Krasniqi, is not an answer to the question. The question is if you take someone for security reasons, one usually has an idea about why there's any need for security at that moment. Could you tell us why you thought that it would be good to have someone there for your security.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I thought when Galan got off the car and ordered me to get on the car alone, I was feeling unsafe. I didn't want to be there alone. And I told Iber Krasniqi, You are coming with me to the place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to -- this was the reason, and I've been repeating it several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you said "I was feeling unsafe." Unsafe for -- because of what or because of whom? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, simply I was not feeling safe, and this was the reason I took him with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was this a kind of, then, unspecific feeling of being unsafe? Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have any fear or not of anyone in that jeep?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No. I simply was feeling ill at ease and I wanted to have somebody with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was Toger's relationship with Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know someone called Aslan?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know someone called Zenun Gashi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Zenun Gashi, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you know Zenun Gashi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, he used to work at the police force of former Yugoslavia, and often we happened to see in the roads, in the village. He was in the village of Baran -- well, I can't say I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say "he was in the village of Baran," was he ever in the military headquarters, where you worked in Baran?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw him?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Only when he was a policeman -- myself, I mean. I saw him when he was in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Kemal Gashi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know him or who he was?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you ever see any Roma in the military barracks in Baran when you were there?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, only soldiers. There were Roma people who were soldiers in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know someone called Selin Kelmendi [phoen] from Kosuric?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there someone called Ramush from Kosuric?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph, it's Exhibit P925. There are two photographs I'm going to show you and I want to ask you if you recognise the scenes in them. The first photograph shows a man taking a photograph near a muddy water course with some trees in the background. Was that the area where Sanije Balaj was shot, her body was buried, and then reburied -- sorry, exhumed. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, but this photograph was taken after the war, not at the time it happened, because at that time this place here was covered in woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we turn to the second photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does that show the wooded area where Sanije Balaj was taken and shot and her body buried?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, it shows a part of it from the place it has been photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you made a statement on the 30th of January, 2006, as a suspect to an international prosecutor, Mr. Robert Dean, in Kosovo. And I asked you before about Toger and feelings or reactions towards Toger. You said something in that statement about feelings and reactions towards Toger. Do you recall what you said there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether or not Mr. Re is seeking to impeach his own witness at this time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- or he's engaged in some other activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it might help us if we would know what portion of that statement you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At the bottom of page 19, the number is R0628908 and ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I speak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. The question was whether you remembered what you said at the time when you gave that statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how you understand this. I repeated this several times. I took him because I did not feel safe, and I was afraid. That's why I took Iber Krasniqi with me, and I remember having said the same thing in that statement. I probably said I was afraid only in the way that you are putting it to me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is who you said you were afraid of which is in that statement. Is it something you've forgotten and which reading this would assist you to -- assist in refreshing your memory?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I mentioned it several times already. I was afraid and I did not want to go alone with them, and there were these three people and that's why I took Iber Krasniqi with me, I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your statement you mention that you were afraid of a person. I'm asking you whether you have forgotten and if reading the statement would refresh your memory as to who it was you said you were afraid of?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's not impeachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He has now indicated on a number of occasions that he remembers what he said in his statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Therefore -- excuse me, Your Honour, if I may finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Therefore, what Mr. Re is doing at this point is impermissible for a number of reasons. The first is that it's leading; the second is that it's been asked and answered, he's got an answer to his question. This witness has not indicated any failure of memory whatsoever. Had he indicated a failure of memory that would be a different matter, but that's not what he's done. He's indicated that he remembers his statement and that's what he said. Now Mr. Re is suggesting that he's forgotten something specific and because he's forgotten something specific he may have a mechanism whereby his memory can be refreshed and that is impermissible. Memory refreshment, that is impeachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He hasn't answered the question. The question was: Have you forgotten it and if so, would reading --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That question has not been clearly answered, Mr. Guy-Smith. The witness referred not to what he said at that time but he referred again and again to what he testified today. And the question on whether -- but let me just see. Mr. Krasniqi, you heard Mr. Re asking you whether you do or whether you do not remember anymore what you said at the time when you gave that statement which is available to the parties. And Mr. Re indicated that you specified a person people would be afraid of. Do you remember that you said such a thing at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell us then what exactly you said at that time about a person people would be afraid of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, of course Togeri.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you say that people would be afraid of Togeri?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, people were afraid of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why were they afraid of him?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I mentioned earlier -- how did you know that people were afraid of him?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, it was said so. They were afraid. Maybe they did not have any reason to, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were these people you're talking about, civilians or military people or a mixture?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Things that were said when people sat together and talked. They said things like this, that they were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were the reasons they were giving for their fear of Toger?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are we now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He's answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Just for one moment go back to Zenun Gashi. What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He was Roma.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. It is close to time for a break, but I know that Mr. Harvey would like to address the Chamber for a minute, not in the presence of the witness, but I'd like to be informed about what the order of cross-examination will be after the break. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think I shall cross-examine first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You cross-examine first.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I will follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll follow --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- unless Mr. Harvey wishes to go --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. Harvey doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Doesn't. Then could you give us a time estimate?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would expect cross-examination to take a little time in combination as between myself and Mr. Guy-Smith. And may we give you a precise time after the break, but I would think it inconceivable that one has directed us to do so that we could complete cross-examination today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If need be --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would concur in that assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Krasniqi, we'll have a break. There's another procedural issue which is not in any way relating to you which the Chamber would like to hear. So therefore, would you already follow Madam Usher, who will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, there was something about witness scheduling which you would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you had asked me to provide you with a response after the last break on the scheduling of (redacted). I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sorry, are we in open --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: There are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would like -- you would give an answer on the videolink scheduled for the 20th of November, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, that was what you asked me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least what the request was --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that the scheduling would be the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I raised an additional concern with Mr. Re before I went to speak with my client, which is whether Witness 30 might be rescheduled for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And whether if the Prosecution were unable to reschedule Witness 30 for tomorrow that would be it as far as they were concerned or whether there might be any attempt to reschedule him for some time next week. I understand from Mr. Re that his attitude is they do not wish to let that witness go and want to pursue him by all means available to them. I at this stage have no idea whether there is any potential for that witness to be called tomorrow. If not, whether the Prosecution intends to make an application to have him videolinked next week. Those matters are inextricably linked as far as my client and I are concerned because it is inconceivable that my client would agree to what are arguably the two most important witnesses in the case against him being taken in a week where his senior counsel cannot be here. So I am in their hands to some extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The updated information I've just got actually this moment is the -- can we move into private session for one moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll have a break until 6.00, but we'll then move into private session immediately, although not for a very long time I take it. We resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we turn into private session I'd like to ask the Defence to respond on P1181, which is the slimmed-down exhibit to complete the verification by Friday, this Friday, at noon --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the same that if there are any -- to verify the redactions of the 92 ter statement of Witness 69 by this Friday, noon, as well. This is a more friendly way of setting deadlines, yes, but of course it's the same. Then we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The first letter request of information concerning prior convictions of witnesses was sent by me in November of 2006. I'm not sure that the Chamber has a copy of that letter and whether that was one of the letters that was actually in the letters that was submitted during the UNMIK hearing that we had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that was at the time it was filed, and you referred to that letter in your recent correspondence with Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Having heard what Mr. Re just said, I would only alert to the Court to the fact that the motion for this witness to be added as a witness was in September of this year. So if we take the assertion made by Mr. Re that they begin their search shortly before a witness is to come and they have been in a position at least for two months to deal with this information which would have perhaps given us a chance to deal with this. And thirdly, and lastly, this is clearly a systemic problem that we have been dealing with throughout this trial and I must say that it has caused an extreme burden on the Defence and an extreme hardship for purposes of adequate and proper preparation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With all the prejudicial concerns that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I suggest to the parties that we do not enter into further debate on this matter at this moment and that we -- not to say that it's not justified that Mr. Re gives his reasons for the late disclosure and that you give the reasons why it should have been done differently. That's now clearly on the record. I'd like the witness to be called in again so that he can be cross-examined. Madam Usher. Yes, then there's another matter which I'd like to raise. In view of what Mr. Harvey told us before the break and in view of many, many uncertainties - and when I'm talking about uncertainties, I'm only talking about the uncertainties we are aware of now, I'm not even talking about the uncertainties we might face tomorrow morning or tomorrow at 10.00 or at 11.00 - but in view of all those uncertainties, the Chamber does not rule at this very moment on the motion for the videolink, but allows Mr. Re to continue preparing for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you'll be cross-examined by -- first by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. And may I urge the parties, all parties, that to try to be as efficient as possible and to focus on the most important matters first. Mr. Re, the Chamber noticed that the first hour of the examination covered an area on which we have already quite some evidence, and especially when we are running out of time. The -- such decisions may have an impact on what happens in the very, very near future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there would be any doubt, I was talking about the videolink scheduled for the 20th -- requested to be scheduled for the 20th. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I indicate with Your Honour's comments in mind that where -- if it becomes necessary to cross-examine in relation to either testimony given at the trial in May or in relation to questions and answers given by this witness during a suspect interview, that I shall do so initially without bringing material up on the screen. But if there's any objection that at any point to the content of what's being put, then obviously that can be dealt with in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I want to make sure I've understood, first of all, your position as of the 12th of August, which is the date that I think we're all agreed was the date on which Sanije Balaj disappeared. At that time you were a member of the military police unit of the FARK brigade at Baran, correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And your brother Mete, your late brother Mete, he was also a member of the military police unit of the FARK brigade at Baran, correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Iber -- can I be clear, is Iber your brother or your cousin?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Iber is my cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Iber Krasniqi, he was also a member of the military police at Baran, correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I'm just going to put to you one passage from the testimony that you gave when questioned in January of 2006 by the prosecutor in Kosovo. You were asked about the military headquarters in Baran and you said: "Nazif Ramabaja was the general commander of the military and the police, and then under him were Esat Ademi and another person by the last name Draga, Musa is his first name." Is that a correct statement of the position?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you took your orders from Hasan Gashi, who was the commander of the military police at the Baran headquarters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But all of you were under the command of Nazif Ramabaja?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And now I want to ask you some questions about the very end of this sequence of events and the investigation that was conducted into Sanije Balaj's disappearance. First of all, you know, don't you, that there was an investigation set up by the KLA into Sanije Balaj's disappearance?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you were called in for interview by a man called Fadil Nimonaj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you were questioned about your involvement?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: By the time that that interview took place, is it correct that Galani had fled the area to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to put to you a passage from the evidence that you gave at Idriz Gashi's trial, and then I'm going to ask you some questions about it. I'll read it to you slowly so that it can be translated. You said this --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could we have the page number to assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's page 44 of the trial transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "I was not present, but I remember when Gani Gjukaj came with Ramush Haradinaj to find out what had happened. Sanije's family were asking where the corpse was and who killed her. I was not there, but the late Mete Krasniqi told them who killed her ..."

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you learn about that conversation from your late brother Mete?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want, please, to pull up Defence document 1D140026, which is a statement or interview of Gani Gjukaj by UNMIK dated the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, do you intend to tender that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do intend to tender that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it needs a number. Madam Registrar that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be D220, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Marked for identification at the moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, we have the Albanian on the screen I think, and I think we will need to look at the second page of the translation -- of the Albanian original. And I shall just read to you from the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GJUKAJ WAS ASKED
utterances.text: "What do you know about the kidnapping and killing of Sanije?" And he replied: "Family members of Sanije came to me in the next day after Sanije was kidnapped and asked me to go to Vranoc village to get information about this case. They also told me that Mete Krasniqi was involved in the kidnapping. Two, three, or four days after this -- I'm sorry, two, three, or four days after I got this information, I was speaking with Ramush Haradinaj, and after I told him that Mete Krasniqi stopped Sanije, we went to Vranoc where we met Mete. I told Mete about the case, but he didn't give me any exact information. After Ramush Haradinaj insisted with words like 'who let you stopping the people? Why are you stopping the people without any reason?' And the strict question: 'If she is alive, please bring her back immediately or if she is dead return her dead body to her family,' to find the people who did this and give responsibility. "Q. What was the answer of Mete Krasniqi? "A. Mete admitted that Sanije was not alive. During that conversation, Mete mentioned the name of the person who killed Sanije and he was Galani."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll let the translation catch up.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, my question, Mr. Krasniqi, is this: Does that reflect what Mete Krasniqi told you about this conversation with Gani Gjukaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, he did not say all those words to me, but he told me that they were there and he had told them who had killed her, and that was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that they were pressing for information about it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gjukaj has made a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor about these meeting -- about this meeting, in which he describes what took place in the conversation with Mete Krasniqi. And he says that after Mete revealed that Galani was implicated, his statement continues: "Avni Krasniqi then entered the room. Avni did not know whether Mete had confessed. When we found out" -- sorry, "when he found out that we knew that Galani had killed her, he became very upset. He also admitted that Galani had killed her." Do you remember a conversation yourself with Gani Gjukaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, I don't. I don't actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does that mean you're telling us that such a conversation did not occur or that you can't remember one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to move now, please, to the suggestion that you've made that Galani was claiming to be some sort of commander. Now, you told us in your evidence in chief that you did not know who appointed him. I just want to ask you this: Was it Galani himself who claimed to be a commander? Is that where you got the information from?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: May I speak? Is it my turn?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the question to you again. Was it from Galani himself that you heard that he was a commander?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, everybody knew that he was commander of Lugu i Drinit, not only me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we go into private session for just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we please call-up Exhibit P172.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You will recall, Mr. Krasniqi, that passage that I have just read to you concerning reallocation. I'd like you to look at this document, please, if you wouldn't mind. This is a document dated the 7th of July of 1998 which bears a signature of Ramush Haradinaj. And just so that we're clear it's a transfer document and in the English it reads: "Fighter Idriz Gashi from the district of Pec reported to our staff on 4 July at his request he is being transferred for duties to another zone. The above-mentioned fighter is ready to assume his duties immediately." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if you look at the Albanian original, the word that is given for Idriz Gashi throughout this document is "luftetari"; is that the correct pronunciation?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just explain what that word means for us.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: "Luftetar" means a fighter of the liberation army.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As opposed to a commander, you would agree?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, he's a fighter and there's no commander here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. One of the important parts of the account that you've given, Mr. Krasniqi, is that everything that happened that day on the 12th of August you had to do because this man was your commander or you felt he was in command, correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, he was not a commander in Baran, he was a commander in Lugu i Drinit, and that's what he said. We never asked for his ID or anything to know who he was. Because we did not have that right. He was the commander of Lugu i Drinit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Help us about this. He'd slept and eaten at the house you shared with Mete Krasniqi in Vranoc, hadn't he?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in the past, that is, before this incident with Sanije Balaj, he'd borrowed a white Mercedes minivan that belonged to your brother Mete, hadn't he, from time to time?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Before this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're confirming that he did do so before this incident?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, before the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A lot of people claimed to be commanders when they weren't really commanders, didn't they, at this time?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we've heard evidence that your brother, Mete, was referred to as a commander. Mr. Krasniqi, did he go by the name Commander Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Mete was not a commander. He was a policeman. He worked with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did he claim to be a commander? Did he ask people to call him Commander Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know Vesel Dizdari?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He was in the military police at Baran, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Also under the command of Nazif Ramabaja directly I think?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us as to why he might refer to your brother Mete as Commander Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know. I've been with Vesel Dizdari for a very short time during that period, maybe two or three times I met him. I had no relation with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was your brother Mete in a position to give orders to other people in the military police?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, in January of last year, January 2006, you were interviewed by the international prosecutor in Kosovo, Mr. Robert Dean, and I think you know, don't you, that at the time that that interview took place on the 30th of January of 2006 UNMIK had opened a criminal investigation into you in connection with this matter?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you were being interviewed, I think, just two weeks after you had been formally declared a suspect on the 16th of January; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just before you were formally interviewed by Mr. Dean, you had a meeting with him, I think, in his office; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in the course of that meeting he discussed with you the possibility that even though you were a suspect it would be possible for you to be declared a cooperating witness, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he explained to you that that would involve giving you an immunity from prosecution for your potential involvement in Sanije Balaj's disappearance and death, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you told that the reason why there was a suspicion, particularly in relation to the account that you had given, was that the prosecutor in Kosovo had information that two men had been seen dragging Sanije Balaj into the woods, not one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: If I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: -- intervene at this particular point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krasniqi, would you take off your earphones for a second. Mr. Krasniqi, do you understand any English? Apparently not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Not mine, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand what the issue is. Mr. Emmerson, we are close to a point where the questions you put to the witness might trigger an answer which could not be excluded to also pertain to the role of Mr. Krasniqi in these events in which he might incriminate himself. I'm not saying that he will, but at least the issue is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, if I may say so, I understand the suggestion we are getting towards that area. I don't think the question that I had just asked would have that potential because the question was asking him whether he had received information from the prosecutor that that was the reason why he had been suspected, which is simply information as to what had been communicated to him by the prosecutor. But be that as it may I'm very happy for the Trial Chamber to caution the witness at this stage but then in my submission I should be permitted to continue with my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not saying that -- Mr. Pestman, you are aware that there is a Rule that if a witness invokes that the answer he would give would incriminate himself that he can address the Chamber and then the Chamber would decide whether or not he has to answer that question. But then, of course, it's up to the witness finally to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that be the -- in your view the suitable approach to take at this moment, that I inform the witness about his rights under - if I immediately find the Rule - yes, I think it's 90(E).

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: I'll have a look at the appropriate rule in a minute, but it might be interesting to know whether he was actually allowed that status of cooperating witness or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's a question that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the procedure --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let me -- then this will be further explored by Mr. Emmerson in his cross-examination. It does not -- well, it might -- Mr. Emmerson, you say you know the answer, could you already --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, the position is as follows. Mr. Krasniqi was then interviewed as a suspect and gave an account to the prosecutor. Under the relevant provision of the Kosovan criminal procedure law as it stood, there was a six-month period of time during which a person could remain a suspect unless that was extended and that period of time was not extended and the status of cooperating witness is finally only given to those who remain suspects when called to testify. So he was never formally given the status of a cooperating witness. There were discussions about it prior to his first interview. He then gave the interview and after a period of six months --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you well that -- at first let's give some time. Mr. Emmerson, is my understanding then correct - and we're talking about legal matters - that since the six-month period had elapsed and apparently there was no realistic expectation or perhaps even a legal impossibility, that Mr. Krasniqi would regain the position of a suspect, that there was no need for him to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My understanding is I'm not in a position to answer the mediating portion of that question. I have no idea at all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- whether or not it is possible for him become a suspect, let us say if fresh evidence were to emerge. It could well be the case I could imagine certainly in many jurisdictions that if that were to happen that somebody could be redeclared a suspect. But certainly at the time he testified in Kosovo in the trial of Idriz Gashi, he was not then the subject of an ongoing investigation and was called as a witness without cooperating witness status.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's understood. Then I'll -- Mr. Re, anything to be added?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, just a query. The question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness was aware that the reason for being suspected was that there was information that two men --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had been seen dragging --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- had been seen dragging --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now I'm asking Mr. Emmerson through the Trial Chamber, where is there evidence of two men being seen dragging. I just would ask that he point out where exactly the dragging reference is --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be that I've used the word "dragging" too loosely and there's been plenty of evidence based upon information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Accompanying --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- from Zymer Hasanaj --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and from the evidence of the witness yesterday that there was an accusation that two men were involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are -- yes. We are rightly admonished not to speak at the same time. The issue then rather is whether Mr. Krasniqi remained in the car or accompanied --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the -- Mr. Gashi and Sanije Balaj when they left --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll -- we'll continue. Mr. Krasniqi, could you put on your earphones again. Mr. Krasniqi, the last question that was put to you was about why at the time you were suspected of being involved in what happened to Sanije Balaj beyond what you testified, now the reason being that there was information that not one but that two persons accompanied Sanije Balaj out of the car into the wood. Now, I would like to inform you that not necessarily this question but questions that could follow. If you would answer them truthfully, that you might say things that would incriminate yourself. Of course I do not know, but you're the only one who knows. If listening to the question you would consider that if you would answer them, as you gave a solemn declaration, in accordance with the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, that you would incriminate yourself, then you may address me and say that you for that reason would rather not answer that question. Now, if that situation arises, this Chamber has the power to order you, to compel you, to answer that question; but if we would do so, then the testimony would give after we would have ordered you to answer the question cannot be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against you for any other offence than false testimony. So if you're ordered and you would still not tell the truth, then you may be subject to investigation and prosecution for false testimony. So is it clear to you? If you fear that your answer might incriminate yourself, and for that reason if you would like not to answer it, please address me. Yes, Mr. Pestman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Am I correct to understand that he would be, if he were forced to answer a question by the Court, that he would be immune to prosecution by the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's for certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: But not by any other judicial body, including the authorities, legal authorities, in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That -- I think at this moment, but the parties will correct me, is an unresolved question. And therefore, I cannot answer that. What I could do is to explain to Mr. Krasniqi that if we would compel him to testify where he has addressed us, that he is immune -- he's not immune for prosecution, but that testimony could not be used against you if you would be prosecuted before this Tribunal. And I add to that that there is some uncertainty whether such testimony could ever be used elsewhere. A possibility of course would be that such answers would be given in private session, which makes it not -- at least not immediately accessible for other jurisdictions. This is for your information, Mr. Pestman. I'm not saying that this is the final solution, but we would -- we could consider to go into private session for those purposes, although it's not the usual reason to go into private session. And of course I would not do that until after I would have consulted the parties on this legal issue. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I'm looking at the clock --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just indicate on one matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Re asked me to clarify the use of the word "dragging". I think the testimony on the record is two men forcing a woman out of a vehicle and two men taking a woman, so just to be clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- rather than dragging, "forcing" and "taking" were the words that we used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, it's 7.00. It's time to conclude for the day. We would like to see you back tomorrow in the afternoon at a quarter to 4.00 because we'll adjourn since there is an initial appearance scheduled at quarter past 2.00 and since we need some time for changing tapes, et cetera, we'll not resume the testimony in this case until quarter to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't know whether the Trial Chamber would wish in these circumstances to give the normal direction to a witness and/or to modify it in any way, given the present circumstances and the fact that he's legally represented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would give the normal -- you would like to have it --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- given the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I just want it to be clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I do understand. Mr. Krasniqi, you have given testimony today. You'll continue tomorrow. You should not speak with anyone about the testimony already given or testimony still to be given. Mr. Pestman, when the testimony has not been finished, the Chamber deems it inappropriate for counsel to discuss matters with the then-witness. If, however, there would be any specific reason why you need to speak to Mr. Krasniqi which could not wait until tomorrow in the afternoon, you would have to apply for permission; and then of course you would tell us why there's such an urgent need. And we'll then consider whether we allow you to speak with Mr. Krasniqi before he has concluded his testimony, and that would then of course be under the very, very strict condition that you would not speak in any way about the testimony, substance of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: I won't make such an application now, but I cannot exclude that the need will arise tomorrow to make such an application with regards to his right not to incriminate himself with a particular -- with regard to a particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is a -- that is an issue which is at the edge. If there's any specific reason -- if you would have -- if you would have any special wishes for me to inform the witness about his rights in this respect, you could contact me or at least through the Legal Officer. You can make an application, say, I would -- and then please copy that to the parties in this case. Yes. Anything else? If not, then with, again, apologies to interpreters, transcribers, but also I often forget them, security, technicians, we'll adjourn until tomorrow, Thursday, the 15th of November, quarter to 4.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of November, 2007, at 3.45 p.m.
